149	
150	**Overview.** Pinnacle Software Holdings, Inc. (\"Pinnacle,\" the \"Company,\" \"we,\" \"us,\" or \"our\") is a leading provider of cloud-based enterprise resource planning (\"ERP\") and customer relationship management (\"CRM\") solutions designed to serve the needs of mid-market businesses. Our integrated software platform enables organizations to manage their financial operations, supply chains, human capital, customer relationships, and business workflows through a unified, cloud-native architecture.
151	
152	Pinnacle was incorporated in the State of Delaware on June 12, 2014. The Company is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional offices in San Jose, California, London, United Kingdom, and Singapore. We completed our initial public offering (\"IPO\") on September 17, 2021, and our shares of common stock trade on the NASDAQ Global Select Market under the ticker symbol \"PNSL.\"
153	
154	Since our founding, we have been dedicated to simplifying the complex operational challenges that mid-market enterprises face when managing their business-critical processes. Unlike legacy on-premises ERP and CRM vendors that require substantial upfront capital expenditures and ongoing maintenance investments, our platform delivers a modern, multi-tenant software-as-a-service (\"SaaS\") experience that can be rapidly deployed and easily scaled. Our subscription-based pricing model provides customers with predictable costs while affording us significant revenue visibility and recurring revenue streams.
155	
156	As of December 31, 2024, we had 2,847 employees globally and served thousands of mid-market businesses across a diverse range of industries, including manufacturing, professional services, healthcare, financial services, technology, and retail. Our market capitalization was approximately \$4.2 billion based on recent trading prices.
157	
158	Our founder, Marcus J. Ellsworth, has served as Chairman of the Board of Directors and Chief Executive Officer since the Company\'s inception in 2014. Mr. Ellsworth\'s vision of delivering enterprise-grade technology to mid-market organizations at an accessible price point has been the driving force behind our product development philosophy and go-to-market strategy.
159	
160	For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, we generated total revenue of \$612.3 million, representing a 22.8% increase from \$498.7 million in the prior year. Our growth has been driven by strong demand for our cloud-based ERP and CRM solutions, expansion of our customer base, increased adoption of our predictive analytics capabilities following the acquisition of DataForge Analytics, Inc. (\"DataForge\") in July 2023, and the continued growth of our international operations.
161	
162	**Our Products and Solutions**
163	
164	We offer a comprehensive suite of cloud-based enterprise software solutions that are purpose-built for mid-market businesses. Our product portfolio consists of the following principal offerings:
165	
166	**Cloud-Based ERP Platform.** Our ERP platform provides a fully integrated set of applications designed to help mid-market organizations manage their core business processes. Key modules within our ERP platform include:
167	
168	> • *Financial Management.* General ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, cash management, budgeting, and financial reporting and consolidation.
169	>
170	> • *Supply Chain Management.* Inventory management, order management, procurement, warehouse management, and demand planning.
171	>
172	> • *Human Capital Management.* Payroll processing, benefits administration, time and attendance tracking, talent management, and workforce planning.
173	
174	Our ERP platform is designed to serve as a single source of truth for mid-market enterprises, eliminating the data silos and manual processes that characterize legacy on-premises systems. The platform supports multi-entity, multi-currency, and multi-language configurations, enabling customers with international operations to manage their global businesses on a unified platform.
175	
176	**CRM Platform.** Our CRM platform empowers sales, marketing, and customer service teams to manage the complete customer lifecycle. Key capabilities include:
177	
178	> • *Sales Automation.* Lead and opportunity management, pipeline forecasting, territory management, quota management, and guided selling workflows.
179	>
180	> • *Marketing Automation.* Campaign management, email marketing, lead scoring, marketing analytics, and customer segmentation.
181	>
182	> • *Customer Service.* Case management, knowledge base, self-service portal, service level agreement tracking, and omnichannel support.
183	>
184	> • *Workflow Automation.* Business process automation, approval workflows, document management, and custom application development.
185	
186	**DataForge Analytics and Predictive Analytics Capabilities.** On July 1, 2023, the Company completed the acquisition of DataForge Analytics, Inc. (\"DataForge\"), a predictive analytics startup based in San Jose, California, for total consideration of \$145.0 million. The acquisition consideration consisted of \$110.0 million in cash and \$35.0 million in Pinnacle common stock, representing 823,529 shares valued at \$42.50 per share at the date of issuance. DataForge\'s predictive analytics and machine learning capabilities have been fully integrated into both our ERP and CRM platforms, enabling our customers to leverage AI-driven insights for a variety of use cases, including:
187	
188	> • *Demand Forecasting.* Utilizing historical data and external signals to predict future demand patterns, enabling more efficient inventory management and production planning.
189	>
190	> • *Customer Churn Prediction.* Identifying at-risk customer accounts and recommending targeted retention strategies using behavioral and engagement data.
191	>
192	> • *Revenue Optimization.* Analyzing pricing sensitivity, cross-sell and upsell propensity, and customer lifetime value to maximize revenue generation.
193	>
194	> • *Operational Efficiency.* Detecting anomalies in operational workflows, predicting equipment maintenance needs, and recommending process improvements.
195	
196	The integration of DataForge significantly expanded Pinnacle\'s total addressable market by adding advanced AI and machine learning capabilities that complement our core ERP and CRM product offerings. At the time of acquisition, DataForge had 127 employees, including a team of approximately 45 data scientists and machine learning engineers who have been retained and integrated into our San Jose engineering center.
197	
198	**Professional Services.** We offer a comprehensive suite of professional services to help customers implement, configure, and optimize their use of our platform. Our professional services include:
199	
200	> • Implementation and deployment services
201	>
202	> • System configuration and customization
203	>
204	> • Data migration from legacy systems
205	>
206	> • Training and education programs
207	>
208	> • Ongoing technical support and managed services
209	
210	**Platform Architecture.** Our platform is built on a modern, multi-tenant SaaS architecture that is hosted on leading public cloud infrastructure. This architecture provides our customers with high availability, scalability, and security while enabling us to deliver continuous updates and new features without requiring customer-side installations or downtime.
211	
212	**Subscription Revenue Model.** Our primary revenue stream is subscription fees charged under annual and multi-year contracts. Subscription pricing is based on the number of users, modules deployed, and the volume of data processed through our analytics capabilities. This model provides us with strong revenue visibility and predictable recurring revenue streams.
213	
214	**Our Market Opportunity**
215	
216	The global market for mid-market ERP and CRM software is substantial and growing. According to industry estimates, the combined mid-market ERP and CRM software market is expected to exceed \$85 billion by 2027, driven by the ongoing migration from on-premises legacy systems to cloud-based solutions. Mid-market enterprises, which we generally define as organizations with between 100 and 5,000 employees and annual revenues ranging from \$50 million to \$2 billion, represent a large and underserved segment of the enterprise software market.
217	
218	Many mid-market organizations continue to rely on aging on-premises ERP and CRM systems that are costly to maintain, difficult to customize, and unable to support modern business requirements such as real-time analytics, mobile access, and cross-functional workflow automation. The growing complexity of business operations, increasing regulatory requirements, and rising customer expectations are driving mid-market enterprises to seek modern, cloud-based alternatives.
219	
220	Our expansion into predictive analytics through the DataForge acquisition further broadens our market opportunity by enabling us to address the growing demand for AI-driven business intelligence and decision-support tools. Additionally, our international expansion into European and Asia-Pacific markets, through our London and Singapore offices, positions us to capture demand in regions where cloud ERP and CRM adoption among mid-market enterprises is accelerating.
221	
222	**Our Growth Strategy**
223	
224	Our growth strategy is centered on the following key pillars:
225	
226	**Expand Our Customer Base in the Mid-Market Segment.** We intend to continue investing in our sales and marketing organization to attract new mid-market customers. Our go-to-market approach combines direct sales with strategic channel partnerships and digital marketing to efficiently reach our target market.
227	
228	**Cross-Sell and Upsell DataForge Predictive Analytics.** The integration of DataForge\'s predictive analytics capabilities into our ERP and CRM platforms creates significant cross-sell and upsell opportunities within our existing customer base. Many of our existing customers have expressed interest in leveraging AI-driven insights, and we have developed targeted sales motions to drive adoption of our analytics offerings.
229	
230	**International Expansion.** We opened our London, United Kingdom office in the second quarter of 2023 and our Singapore office in the first quarter of 2024 to support our expansion into European and Asia-Pacific markets, respectively. We intend to continue building our international sales, customer success, and support capabilities to serve the growing demand for cloud-based ERP and CRM solutions in these regions.
231	
232	**Continue R&D Investment in AI and Machine Learning Capabilities.** We believe that artificial intelligence and machine learning will be critical differentiators in the enterprise software market. We intend to continue investing in our DataForge technology stack and broader AI/ML capabilities to maintain our competitive edge and expand the range of intelligent features available to our customers.
233	
234	**Selective Strategic Acquisitions.** We intend to selectively pursue strategic acquisitions that complement our existing product offerings, expand our technology capabilities, or accelerate our entry into new markets. The successful acquisition and integration of DataForge in 2023 demonstrates our ability to identify, execute, and integrate value-accretive acquisitions.
235	
236	**Customers.** As of December 31, 2024, we served thousands of mid-market businesses across diverse industries, including manufacturing, professional services, healthcare, financial services, technology, retail, and non-profit organizations. No single customer accounted for more than 2% of our total revenue in FY2024.
237	
238	Our net revenue retention rate for FY2024 was approximately 118%, reflecting the strong expansion activity within our existing customer base, including upsells of additional modules, increased user counts, and adoption of DataForge predictive analytics capabilities. Our gross revenue retention rate was approximately 93%, reflecting our strong customer satisfaction and the mission-critical nature of our software platform.
239	
240	Approximately 1,200 customer accounts were affected by the cybersecurity incident disclosed in October 2024. For further information regarding this incident, see \"Item 1C. Cybersecurity\" below.
241	
242	**Technology and Development**
243	
244	We invested \$128.7 million in research and development during FY2024, representing approximately 21.0% of total revenue. Our R&D investments are focused on enhancing our core ERP and CRM platform, expanding the capabilities of our DataForge predictive analytics engine, developing new AI and machine learning features, and improving the overall user experience.
245	
246	Our engineering teams are primarily located at our Austin, Texas headquarters and our San Jose, California engineering center. The San Jose facility serves as the primary hub for our DataForge machine learning and data science teams. Dr. Priya Venkatesh was appointed as our Chief Technology Officer on August 1, 2023, to lead our overall technology strategy, including the integration and advancement of the DataForge technology stack.
247	
248	Our technology platform leverages modern cloud-native architecture, microservices, containerization, and advanced data processing frameworks. We continuously invest in the reliability, scalability, and security of our platform to meet the demanding requirements of our enterprise customers.
249	
250	**Competition.** The mid-market ERP and CRM software market is competitive and subject to rapid technological change. We compete with a range of companies, including:
251	
252	> • Large enterprise software vendors such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, and Salesforce, which offer ERP and CRM solutions that serve both large enterprise and mid-market segments.
253	>
254	> • Mid-market focused ERP and CRM vendors that offer specialized solutions for specific industries or business functions.
255	>
256	> • Emerging SaaS and cloud-based vendors that are entering the mid-market with innovative, AI-driven platforms.
257	
258	We believe we compete favorably based on our purpose-built mid-market focus, the breadth and integration of our ERP and CRM platform, our predictive analytics capabilities following the DataForge acquisition, our modern cloud-native architecture, our subscription-based pricing model, and our strong customer satisfaction metrics. However, many of our larger competitors have significantly greater financial, technical, and marketing resources, and the increasing investment by competitors in artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities represents a significant competitive risk.
259	
260	**Intellectual Property.** We rely on a combination of patents, trademarks, copyrights, trade secrets, and contractual restrictions to protect our intellectual property and proprietary technology. As of December 31, 2024, we held 23 issued U.S. patents and had 11 pending patent applications relating to various aspects of our ERP, CRM, and analytics technology. Our issued patents have expiration dates ranging from 2032 to 2042.
261	
262	We also rely on trademark protection for our brand names and logos, including the \"Pinnacle\" and \"DataForge\" marks. We protect our trade secrets through confidentiality and invention assignment agreements with our employees and contractors.
263	
264	For information regarding the patent infringement litigation filed by Veritech Solutions LLC, see \"Item 3. Legal Proceedings\" below.
265	
266	**Government Regulation and Compliance**
267	
268	Our business is subject to a variety of laws and regulations in the jurisdictions in which we operate. As a provider of cloud-based software that processes and stores customer data, we are subject to data privacy and protection regulations, including the European Union\'s General Data Protection Regulation (\"GDPR\") applicable to our London operations and the Personal Data Protection Act (\"PDPA\") applicable to our Singapore operations.
269	
270	As a public company listed on the NASDAQ Global Select Market, we are subject to the reporting requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, the rules and regulations of the SEC (including the cybersecurity disclosure rules that became effective in December 2023), and the listing standards of the NASDAQ Stock Market.
271	
272	**Human Capital.** As of December 31, 2024, we had 2,847 employees, consisting of:
273	
274	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
275	  **Function**                                 **Headcount**
276	  -------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
277	  Research and Development                     1,142
278	
279	  Sales and Marketing                          843
280	
281	  Professional Services and Customer Support   512
282	
283	  General and Administrative                   350
284	
285	  **Total**                                    **2,847**
286	  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
287	
288	Our employees are located across our four offices: Austin, Texas (approximately 1,650 employees); San Jose, California (approximately 710 employees, including employees from the DataForge acquisition); London, United Kingdom (approximately 285 employees); and Singapore (approximately 202 employees). At the time of the DataForge acquisition on July 1, 2023, approximately 127 DataForge employees joined the Company.
289	
290	We believe our employees are our most valuable asset. We offer competitive compensation packages, including base salary, performance-based cash incentive awards, and equity-based compensation under our 2021 Equity Incentive Plan. None of our employees are represented by a labor union, and we consider our employee relations to be good.
291	
292	**Seasonality.** Our subscription-based revenue model provides us with strong revenue visibility throughout the year. However, our business experiences some seasonality, with the fourth quarter historically being our strongest quarter for new customer bookings and contract renewals. This seasonality is consistent with the general enterprise software industry trend of year-end purchasing cycles.
293	
294	**Available Information.** Our Annual Reports on Form 10-K, Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q, Current Reports on Form 8-K, proxy statements, and amendments to those reports are available free of charge through our website at www.pinnaclesoftware.com as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such materials with, or furnish them to, the SEC. These reports are also available on the SEC\'s website at www.sec.gov. Our CIK Number is 0001847293. The information contained on, or that can be accessed through, our website is not incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
295	
296	**[Item 1A. Risk Factors]{.underline}**
297	
298	*Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following risk factors, together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes thereto, before investing in our common stock. The occurrence of any of the following risks could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects. In such case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. The risks described below are not the only risks facing the Company. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial may also materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We have organized the following 34 risk factors by category for ease of reference.*
299	
300	**Risks Related to Our Business and Operations**
301

1	**Risks Related to Our Business and Operations**
2	
3	**Our subscription-based revenue model depends on customer retention and expansion, and a decline in our customer retention rate could adversely affect our revenue and results of operations.** Our subscription-based revenue model is dependent upon our ability to retain existing customers and expand their use of our platform. Our customers are not obligated to renew their subscription contracts upon expiration, and we cannot assure you that our customers will renew at the same or higher service levels, or at all. If our customers do not renew their subscriptions, or if they reduce their usage of our platform, our revenue and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. Our net revenue retention rate, which was approximately 118% for FY2024, could decline in future periods due to customer dissatisfaction, competitive alternatives, changes in customer budgets, general economic conditions, or other factors.
4	
5	**We face intense competition in the ERP and CRM markets, including from competitors with substantially greater resources.** The markets for ERP and CRM software are intensely competitive and subject to rapid technological change. We compete with large, well-established enterprise software vendors such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft, and Salesforce, as well as a growing number of mid-market focused and emerging SaaS vendors. Many of our competitors have significantly greater financial, technical, marketing, and other resources than we do, as well as larger customer bases, more extensive partner ecosystems, and greater brand recognition. If we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
6	
7	**Competitors are investing heavily in artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities, and our AI-driven predictive analytics features may not keep pace with technological advancements.** The enterprise software industry is increasingly focused on artificial intelligence and machine learning as a key competitive differentiator. Large technology companies, including our existing competitors and new market entrants, are making significant investments in AI and machine learning capabilities. Although we have invested substantially in AI-driven predictive analytics through our acquisition of DataForge Analytics, Inc. and continued internal R&D investment, there can be no assurance that our AI and machine learning features will keep pace with the rapid advancements being made by competitors with greater resources. If our customers perceive our AI capabilities as inferior to those of our competitors, or if new AI-driven technologies disrupt the ERP and CRM markets in ways that we are unable to address, our competitive position, business, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
8	
9	**We depend on third-party cloud infrastructure providers, and any disruption in the services provided by these third parties could adversely affect our business.** Our platform is hosted on third-party public cloud infrastructure. We do not control the operation of these third-party facilities. Any disruptions, outages, or security incidents affecting these cloud infrastructure providers could impair the delivery of our platform and harm our reputation and business.
10	
11	**Our ability to attract and retain qualified employees, particularly in software engineering and data science, is critical to our success.** Our future success depends on our ability to attract, retain, and motivate highly skilled employees, particularly software engineers, data scientists, machine learning researchers, product managers, and sales professionals. Competition for qualified employees in the technology industry is intense, and we may be unable to attract and retain the personnel we need.
12	
13	**We have experienced significant management transitions, and any future management changes could disrupt our business. The Company has experienced significant management changes in recent periods, including the appointment of Jennifer Tsao-Park as Chief Financial Officer in March 2023, Dr. Priya Venkatesh as Chief Technology Officer in August 2023, and Daniel K. Moretti as General Counsel in January 2024. While we believe these transitions have been successfully managed, management transitions involve risks, including potential disruptions to operations, strategic direction, and employee morale. Any future departures of key members of our management team could disrupt our business and adversely affect our results of operations.**
14	
15	**Risks Related to the DataForge Acquisition and Strategic Transactions**
16	
17	**The integration of DataForge Analytics, Inc. involves risks that could adversely affect our business and financial results.** The Company completed the acquisition of DataForge Analytics, Inc. on July 1, 2023, for total consideration of \$145.0 million (\$110.0 million in cash and \$35.0 million in the Company\'s common stock). The integration of acquired businesses involves significant risks, including the retention of key personnel, the integration of technology platforms and product offerings, the realization of anticipated synergies and revenue opportunities, the diversion of management\'s attention from other business activities, and the potential for unforeseen liabilities or integration costs. We recorded goodwill of \$89.2 million and identifiable intangible assets of \$43.5 million in connection with the DataForge acquisition, which are subject to periodic impairment testing. If the expected benefits of the acquisition are not realized, or if we are required to record impairment charges related to the acquired goodwill or intangible assets, our financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
18	
19	**We may pursue additional acquisitions in the future, which involve inherent risks and uncertainties.** As part of our growth strategy, we may pursue additional acquisitions of businesses, technologies, or assets. Acquisitions involve inherent risks, including difficulties in integrating acquired operations, the potential loss of key employees of acquired companies, the assumption of unknown liabilities, and the diversion of management resources. We cannot assure you that any future acquisitions will be completed on favorable terms or that they will be successfully integrated.
20	
21	**Risks Related to Cybersecurity and Data Privacy**
22	
23	**We have experienced, and may in the future experience, cybersecurity incidents that could materially adversely affect our business, reputation, and financial results.** In October 2024, the Company experienced a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to certain customer-facing systems that affected approximately 1,200 customer accounts. The incident was disclosed in a Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC on October 28, 2024. The Company promptly activated its incident response plan, engaged third-party cybersecurity forensic experts, notified all affected customers, and provided credit monitoring services. The Company completed its remediation efforts by December 2024, including patching of affected systems, implementation of enhanced monitoring capabilities, and deployment of additional security controls.
24	
25	The incident resulted in incremental costs of approximately \$4.2 million for investigation, remediation, customer notification, and credit monitoring services during FY2024. While the Company believes the incident has been fully remediated, there can be no assurance that additional vulnerabilities will not be discovered, that the Company will not be subject to future cybersecurity incidents, or that existing or future security measures will be adequate to prevent or mitigate future attacks. Cybersecurity incidents could result in significant financial losses, regulatory penalties, reputational harm, loss of customer confidence, and litigation. The frequency, sophistication, and severity of cybersecurity attacks on technology companies continues to increase, and we may be unable to prevent all such incidents.
26	
27	The Company is subject to an increasing number of laws, regulations, and industry standards regarding data privacy and cybersecurity, including the SEC\'s cybersecurity disclosure rules that became effective in December 2023, which require disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents and cybersecurity risk management, strategy, and governance. Compliance with these evolving requirements imposes additional costs and may increase our exposure to liability.
28	
29	**We are subject to data privacy regulations that may impose significant costs and operational constraints.** Our operations are subject to data privacy regulations in the jurisdictions in which we operate, including the General Data Protection Regulation (\"GDPR\") in the European Union (applicable to our London operations) and the Personal Data Protection Act (\"PDPA\") in Singapore. These regulations impose significant obligations relating to the collection, use, storage, and transfer of personal data, and non-compliance could result in substantial fines and penalties.
30	
31	**Risks Related to International Operations**
32	
33	**Our international expansion subjects us to additional risks and uncertainties.** We have expanded our international operations through the opening of our London, United Kingdom office in the second quarter of 2023 and our Singapore office in the first quarter of 2024. International operations subject us to additional risks, including exposure to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations, compliance with foreign laws and regulations (including data privacy, employment, and tax laws), political and economic instability, difficulties in managing operations across multiple time zones and geographies, and potential adverse tax consequences. Our international revenue currently represents a small but growing portion of our total revenue, and the risks associated with international operations could become more significant as our international business expands.
34	
35	**Risks Related to Intellectual Property and Litigation**
36	
37	**We are subject to patent infringement litigation that, if resolved unfavorably, could result in substantial damages or other remedies.** On April 12, 2024, Veritech Solutions LLC (\"Veritech\") filed a patent infringement lawsuit against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas (Case No. 6:24-cv-00387), alleging that certain features of our CRM workflow automation tools infringe two U.S. patents held by Veritech. Veritech is seeking damages of \$75.0 million, along with injunctive relief, attorneys\' fees, and costs. The Company filed its answer on June 10, 2024, denying all allegations of infringement and asserting affirmative defenses of invalidity and non-infringement. While the Company believes these claims are without merit and intends to vigorously defend the matter, an unfavorable outcome could require payment of substantial damages, entry of injunctive relief that could prevent us from offering certain features of our CRM platform, or require us to enter into licensing arrangements on unfavorable terms. See \"Item 3. Legal Proceedings\" for additional information.
38	
39	**Our business may be adversely affected by claims of intellectual property infringement.** The software industry is characterized by frequent claims of intellectual property infringement. We may in the future receive additional claims alleging that our products infringe the intellectual property rights of third parties. The defense of such claims, regardless of merit, could be time-consuming, costly, and divert management attention from our business operations.
40	
41	**Risks Related to Financial Condition and Indebtedness**
42	
43	**Our indebtedness under our senior secured credit facility could adversely affect our financial flexibility and results of operations.** As of December 31, 2024, we had \$225.0 million in outstanding indebtedness under the Term Loan B component of our \$400.0 million senior secured credit facility with Calverley National Bank, as administrative agent. Our indebtedness could limit our ability to obtain additional financing, make capital expenditures, or pursue strategic acquisitions, and could increase our vulnerability to adverse economic and industry conditions. The credit facility contains financial covenants and other restrictions that may limit our operational and financial flexibility.
44	
45	**We are exposed to interest rate risk on our variable rate indebtedness.** Borrowings under our credit facility bear interest at a floating rate equal to SOFR plus 2.75%, subject to a SOFR floor of 0.50%. Increases in the Secured Overnight Financing Rate could increase our interest expense and adversely affect our financial results. A 100 basis point increase in SOFR would increase our annual interest expense by approximately \$2.25 million based on current outstanding borrowings.
46	
47	**Our credit facility contains restrictive covenants that may limit our ability to operate our business.** Our credit facility requires us to maintain a Total Net Leverage Ratio of no greater than 4.50:1.00 and an Interest Coverage Ratio of no less than 3.00:1.00. If we fail to comply with these covenants, the lenders could declare all outstanding amounts immediately due and payable, which could have a material adverse effect on our business and financial condition.
48	
49	**Adverse macroeconomic and interest rate conditions could negatively affect our business and financial results.** Our business and the businesses of our mid-market customers are affected by general macroeconomic conditions. Economic downturns, rising interest rates, inflation, or other adverse macroeconomic conditions could reduce demand for our products and services, impair the financial condition of our customers, and increase our operating costs.
50	
51	**Risks Related to Our Common Stock**
52	
53	**Our stock price may be volatile, which could result in substantial losses for investors.** The trading price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly in response to a variety of factors, including our quarterly financial results, changes in financial estimates by securities analysts, changes in our customer base or revenue growth, cybersecurity incidents, litigation developments, general market conditions, and other factors.
54	
55	**Future sales or issuances of our common stock, or the perception thereof, could dilute existing stockholders.** The issuance of additional shares of common stock, including shares issued under our 2021 Equity Incentive Plan, in connection with future acquisitions, or pursuant to shelf registration statements, could dilute the ownership interests of existing stockholders and adversely affect the per-share trading price of our common stock.
56	
57	**Anti-takeover provisions in our certificate of incorporation and bylaws, and under Delaware law, could discourage or prevent a change of control transaction.** Our amended and restated certificate of incorporation and amended and restated bylaws contain provisions that could make it more difficult for a third party to acquire us. These provisions include a classified board of directors, restrictions on the ability of stockholders to call special meetings, and advance notice requirements for stockholder proposals and director nominations. In addition, as a Delaware corporation, we are subject to Section 203 of the Delaware General Corporation Law, which may further discourage takeover attempts.
58	
59	**General Risk Factors**
60	
61	**Changes in macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, recession, or disruptions in the financial markets, could adversely affect our business.** Our business and the businesses of our mid-market customers are sensitive to changes in general economic conditions. Prolonged economic downturns could result in reduced IT spending, longer sales cycles, and increased customer churn.
62	
63	**Changes in tax laws and regulations, or adverse determinations by tax authorities, could adversely affect our financial results.** We are subject to income taxes in the United States and, increasingly, in foreign jurisdictions. Changes in tax laws, regulations, or their interpretation, including potential increases in corporate tax rates, could materially increase our tax liability and adversely affect our net income.
64	
65	**Changes in laws, regulations, or accounting standards could increase our costs and adversely affect our operations.** Our business is subject to various federal, state, and foreign laws and regulations, as well as evolving accounting standards. Changes in these laws, regulations, or standards could increase our compliance costs, impose additional obligations on our business, and adversely affect our operations and financial results.
66	
67	**[Item 1B. Unresolved Staff Comments]{.underline}**
68	
69	None.
70	
71	**[Item 1C. Cybersecurity]{.underline}**
72	
73	**Cybersecurity Risk Management and Strategy**
74	
75	The Company maintains a comprehensive cybersecurity risk management program that is integrated into its overall enterprise risk management framework. Our cybersecurity program is designed to identify, assess, mitigate, and manage cybersecurity risks that could materially affect our business operations, financial condition, and the security and availability of our platform and customer data.
76	
77	Our cybersecurity risk management processes include the following key elements:
78	
79	> • *Risk Assessments.* We conduct regular cybersecurity risk assessments, including annual enterprise-wide risk assessments and targeted assessments of critical systems and applications. These assessments are designed to identify vulnerabilities, evaluate the effectiveness of our security controls, and prioritize remediation efforts based on risk severity.
80	>
81	> • *Third-Party Security Consultants.* We engage independent third-party cybersecurity consultants to conduct penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and security audits of our systems and infrastructure on at least an annual basis, and more frequently for critical systems.
82	>
83	> • *Employee Training.* All employees are required to complete cybersecurity awareness training upon hire and on an annual basis. Employees with access to sensitive systems receive additional role-based security training. We conduct regular phishing simulation exercises to assess and reinforce employee awareness.
84	>
85	> • *Incident Response Plan.* We maintain a comprehensive cybersecurity incident response plan that establishes procedures for the detection, containment, investigation, remediation, and reporting of cybersecurity incidents. The plan is tested through tabletop exercises conducted at least annually.
86	>
87	> • *Enterprise Risk Management Integration.* Cybersecurity risk is identified as one of the Company\'s top enterprise risks and is assessed and managed through our broader enterprise risk management framework, which includes regular reporting to the Board of Directors and its Audit Committee.
88	
89	**Material Cybersecurity Incident**
90	
91	In October 2024, the Company identified unauthorized access to certain customer-facing systems. The incident affected approximately 1,200 customer accounts and involved the exploitation of a vulnerability in a third-party software component integrated into our CRM platform. Upon detection, the Company promptly activated its cybersecurity incident response plan and took the following actions:
92	
93	> • Engaged a leading third-party cybersecurity forensic firm to assist with the investigation and remediation.
94	>
95	> • Contained the unauthorized access within 48 hours of detection and isolated affected systems.
96	>

**Results of Operations --- FY2024 Compared to FY2023**

**Revenue.** Total revenue increased \$113.6 million, or 22.8%, from \$498.7 million in FY2023 to \$612.3 million in FY2024.

Subscription revenue increased \$95.6 million, or 24.3%, from \$394.2 million in FY2023 to \$489.8 million in FY2024. The increase was primarily driven by new customer additions, expansion of existing customer accounts through cross-sell and upsell activity (including adoption of DataForge predictive analytics features), and the impact of a full year of DataForge subscription revenue in FY2024 compared to a partial year (from the July 1, 2023 acquisition date) in FY2023.

Professional services revenue increased \$18.0 million, or 17.2%, from \$104.5 million in FY2023 to \$122.5 million in FY2024. The increase was driven by implementation services for new customers, DataForge integration and enablement services for existing customers, and increased demand for customization and training services.

**Cost of Revenue.** Total cost of revenue increased from \$180.5 million in FY2023 to \$214.3 million in FY2024. Subscription cost of revenue was \$146.9 million in FY2024, consisting primarily of cloud hosting costs, platform operations and support personnel costs, and amortization of acquired technology. Professional services cost of revenue was \$67.4 million in FY2024, consisting primarily of personnel costs for our professional services and customer success teams. Gross profit was \$398.0 million in FY2024, representing a gross margin of 65.0%, compared to \$318.2 million and 63.8% in FY2023. The improvement in gross margin was driven by operating leverage on subscription revenue and improved efficiency in our professional services organization.

**Research and Development.** Research and development expenses were \$128.7 million in FY2024, compared to \$112.4 million in FY2023. The \$16.3 million increase was driven by increased headcount and personnel costs, including a full year of DataForge engineering team costs, as well as continued investment in AI and machine learning capabilities, new product features, and platform infrastructure.

**Sales and Marketing.** Sales and marketing expenses were \$152.4 million in FY2024, compared to \$124.8 million in FY2023. The \$27.6 million increase reflected investment in expanding our direct sales force, building out our international sales teams in London and Singapore, DataForge go-to-market initiatives, and increased marketing spending to drive brand awareness and demand generation.

**General and Administrative.** General and administrative expenses were \$61.2 million in FY2024, compared to \$50.2 million in FY2023. The \$11.0 million increase included approximately \$4.2 million in costs related to the October 2024 cybersecurity incident investigation, remediation, customer notification, and credit monitoring services, as well as increased litigation defense costs, corporate infrastructure investments, and costs associated with our international expansion.

**Operating Income.** Operating income was \$55.7 million in FY2024, representing an operating margin of 9.1%, compared to operating income of \$30.8 million and an operating margin of 6.2% in FY2023. The improvement in operating margin reflects the benefits of revenue scale and operating leverage, partially offset by increased investment in R&D, sales and marketing, and the incremental costs associated with the cybersecurity incident.

**Interest Expense.** Interest expense was \$8.2 million in FY2024, compared to \$9.1 million in FY2023. The decrease reflected scheduled amortization payments on the Term Loan B, which reduced the outstanding principal balance during the year. Borrowings under the credit facility bear interest at SOFR plus 2.75%.

**Other Income.** Other income was \$2.1 million in FY2024, consisting primarily of interest income on cash and cash equivalents.

**Income Tax Provision.** The income tax provision was \$7.8 million in FY2024, reflecting an effective tax rate of approximately 15.7%. The effective tax rate was lower than the U.S. statutory rate of 21% primarily due to the benefit of research and development tax credits, stock-based compensation deductions, and the tax impact of foreign operations.

**Net Income.** Net income was \$41.8 million in FY2024, compared to \$22.1 million in FY2023. Basic earnings per share was \$0.54, calculated on a weighted average of 77,000,000 basic shares outstanding. Diluted earnings per share was \$0.50, calculated on 84,025,000 weighted average diluted shares outstanding, reflecting the dilutive effect of outstanding stock options and RSUs.

**Liquidity and Capital Resources**

**Cash and Cash Equivalents.** As of December 31, 2024, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of \$187.4 million, compared to \$152.8 million as of December 31, 2023. The Company believes its existing cash, cash equivalents, and available borrowing capacity under its revolving credit facility provide sufficient liquidity to fund its operations for at least the next 12 months.

**Credit Facility.** On March 15, 2022, the Company entered into a \$400.0 million senior secured credit facility (the \"Credit Facility\") with Calverley National Bank, as administrative agent, and the lenders party thereto. The Credit Facility consists of:

> \(i\) a \$250.0 million Term Loan B (the \"Term Loan B\"), which was fully drawn at closing and is subject to quarterly amortization payments equal to 0.25% of the original principal amount; and
>
> \(ii\) a \$150.0 million revolving credit facility (the \"Revolver\"), which may be used for general corporate purposes, including working capital and permitted acquisitions.

As of December 31, 2024, \$225.0 million was outstanding under the Term Loan B (after scheduled amortization payments), and the Revolver was undrawn. The Credit Facility matures on March 15, 2027.

Borrowings under the Credit Facility bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (\"SOFR\") plus 2.75%, subject to a SOFR floor of 0.50%. The Credit Facility is secured by substantially all of the Company\'s assets and contains customary affirmative and negative covenants, as well as the following financial covenants:

> \(a\) a Total Net Leverage Ratio of no greater than 4.50:1.00, tested quarterly; and
>
> \(b\) an Interest Coverage Ratio of no less than 3.00:1.00, tested quarterly.

As of December 31, 2024, the Company\'s Total Net Leverage Ratio was 0.33:1.00, calculated as (\$225.0 million in total debt minus \$187.4 million in cash and cash equivalents) divided by \$112.5 million in Adjusted EBITDA (as defined in the Credit Agreement), well within the applicable covenant threshold. The Company was in compliance with all financial covenants as of December 31, 2024.

**Total Debt and Net Debt.** As of December 31, 2024, total debt was \$225.0 million and net debt (total debt minus cash and cash equivalents) was \$37.6 million.

**Prior Bridge Credit Facility.** The Company\'s prior bridge credit facility in the amount of \$45,000,000 was fully repaid in connection with the closing of the Company\'s IPO in September 2021. The bridge credit facility is no longer outstanding and was terminated upon repayment.

**Critical Accounting Estimates**

The preparation of our consolidated financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. We base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances. Actual results could differ materially from these estimates. We consider the following to be our most critical accounting estimates:

**Revenue Recognition (ASC 606).** We recognize subscription revenue ratably over the contract term, beginning on the date our platform is made available to the customer. Professional services revenue is generally recognized as services are performed or upon completion of deliverables, depending on the nature of the engagement.

**Goodwill Impairment.** We test goodwill for impairment annually as of October 1 and more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of a reporting unit may exceed its fair value. As of December 31, 2024, we had \$89.2 million in goodwill, substantially all of which relates to the DataForge acquisition. No impairment was recorded in FY2024 or FY2023.

**Stock-Based Compensation.** We measure and recognize compensation expense for stock options and restricted stock units based on estimated fair values at the date of grant, using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model for stock options and the closing stock price on the date of grant for RSUs.

**Income Taxes.** We account for income taxes using the asset and liability method, recognizing deferred tax assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities.

**Business Combinations.** We account for business combinations using the acquisition method under ASC 805, which requires that we recognize the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their fair values as of the acquisition date. The excess of the purchase consideration over the fair value of the net identifiable assets acquired is recorded as goodwill.

**[Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk]{.underline}**

**Interest Rate Risk.** Our primary exposure to market risk relates to our variable rate indebtedness under the Credit Facility. As of December 31, 2024, we had \$225.0 million of variable rate borrowings outstanding under the Term Loan B at an interest rate of SOFR plus 2.75%. Based on the outstanding borrowings as of December 31, 2024, a hypothetical increase of 100 basis points in the applicable SOFR rate would increase our annual interest expense by approximately \$2.25 million.

**Foreign Currency Risk.** We are exposed to foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations in connection with our international operations in the United Kingdom and Singapore. Revenue and expenses generated by our London and Singapore offices are denominated primarily in British pounds sterling and Singapore dollars, respectively. As of December 31, 2024, our international revenue represented a relatively small portion of our total revenue, and we have not entered into any foreign currency hedging arrangements. As our international operations grow, our exposure to foreign currency fluctuations may become more significant.

**Commodity Price Risk.** We do not have material exposure to commodity price risk in our operations.

**Note 2 --- Summary of Significant Accounting Policies**

*Revenue Recognition.* The Company recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606, *Revenue from Contracts with Customers*. Subscription revenue is recognized ratably over the contract term beginning when the platform is made available to the customer. Professional services revenue is generally recognized as services are performed.

*Stock-Based Compensation.* Stock-based compensation expense is recognized based on the fair value of stock options and restricted stock units at the date of grant, measured using the Black-Scholes option-pricing model for stock options.

*Goodwill and Intangible Assets.* Goodwill is not amortized but is tested for impairment annually as of October 1, or more frequently if events or circumstances indicate potential impairment. Acquired intangible assets with finite useful lives are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives.

**Note 4 --- Debt**

On March 15, 2022, the Company entered into a \$400.0 million senior secured credit facility (the \"Credit Facility\") with Calverley National Bank, as administrative agent. The Credit Facility consists of a \$250.0 million Term Loan B and a \$150.0 million revolving credit facility. Borrowings bear interest at SOFR plus 2.75%, subject to a SOFR floor of 0.50%. The Credit Facility matures on March 15, 2027, and is secured by substantially all of the Company\'s assets.

As of December 31, 2024, \$225.0 million was outstanding under the Term Loan B (after scheduled quarterly amortization payments of \$625,000), and the revolving credit facility was undrawn. The Credit Facility contains financial covenants requiring maintenance of a Total Net Leverage Ratio of no greater than 4.50:1.00 and an Interest Coverage Ratio of no less than 3.00:1.00. As of December 31, 2024, the Company was in compliance with all covenants.

**Note 5 --- Commitments and Contingencies**

*Veritech Solutions LLC Litigation.* On April 12, 2024, Veritech Solutions LLC filed a patent infringement complaint against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas (Case No. 6:24-cv-00387), alleging infringement of two U.S. patents and seeking damages of \$75.0 million, injunctive relief, attorneys\' fees, and costs. The Company has not recorded any loss contingency related to this matter as it is not considered probable that a loss has been incurred.

**[PROSPECTUS SUMMARY (pp. 1--8 of prospectus)]{.underline}**

**[Overview / Our Business]{.underline}**

Pinnacle Software Holdings, Inc. is a leading provider of cloud-based enterprise resource planning, or ERP, and customer relationship management, or CRM, solutions purpose-built for mid-market businesses. We founded Pinnacle in 2014 to address what we believed was a significant gap in the software market: the lack of a unified, cloud-native platform designed specifically for organizations that had outgrown entry-level software but did not require, or could not effectively implement, the complexity and cost of traditional enterprise suites. Since our inception, we have focused on delivering modern, configurable applications that help mid-market companies manage core business functions across finance, supply chain, human capital, sales, marketing, customer service, and internal workflow automation.

Our founder, Marcus J. Ellsworth, launched the business after observing that many mid-market enterprises were operating with fragmented systems, duplicative workflows, and limited real-time visibility into operations. From the beginning, our strategy has been to provide a single platform that unifies operational and customer-facing workflows while remaining easier to deploy, administer, and scale than legacy alternatives. We believe our software enables customers to improve decision-making, reduce manual processes, accelerate implementation timelines, and support growth without the need to replace multiple disconnected applications.

Our product portfolio consists of two integrated solution families. Our cloud ERP suite includes financial management, supply chain management, and human capital management functionality, as well as project management capabilities for customers in services-oriented industries. Our CRM platform includes sales automation, marketing automation, customer service, and workflow automation tools designed to support both demand generation and post-sale engagement. These applications are delivered as software-as-a-service, or SaaS, through a multi-tenant cloud architecture, enabling customers to benefit from rapid innovation cycles, recurring feature releases, centralized security controls, and lower on-premise infrastructure requirements.

We primarily serve mid-market enterprises with 200 to 5,000 employees across a range of verticals, including manufacturing, distribution, professional services, healthcare, and technology. We believe these industries often have complex workflows and regulatory or reporting needs, yet remain underserved by software providers that tend to focus either on small businesses or the largest global enterprises. We have designed our applications and implementation processes to accommodate this market segment\'s need for flexibility, rapid time-to-value, and cost discipline.

Our revenue model is primarily subscription-based. We enter into annual and multi-year software subscription agreements that generate recurring revenue and high visibility into future performance. We supplement subscription revenue with professional services revenue related to implementation, training, configuration, and limited customization work. While professional services revenue generally carries lower gross margins than subscription revenue, we view these services as an important enabler of customer success and long-term expansion opportunities.

We believe several competitive strengths differentiate our business. First, our solutions are purpose-built for the mid-market, which we believe allows us to offer a better balance of functionality, configurability, and ease of use than many alternatives. Second, our customers benefit from a single unified platform rather than disconnected point solutions, which can reduce integration costs and simplify administration. Third, our cloud-native, multi-tenant architecture enables us to deploy enhancements rapidly and operate at scale. Fourth, we have built an implementation methodology and customer success model designed to drive adoption and retention. As of June 30, 2021, our net revenue retention rate was 118%, reflecting our ability to expand customer relationships over time.

As of June 30, 2021, we had over 2,400 customers and approximately 1,850 employees. Our employees include software engineers, product managers, implementation consultants, customer support personnel, sales professionals, and corporate staff. Our principal executive offices are located in Austin, Texas, and we maintain an engineering presence in San Jose, California.

We sell our solutions through a combination of direct sales, inside sales, and an ecosystem of implementation and reseller partners. Our go-to-market strategy emphasizes a land-and-expand approach, with many customers initially adopting one or two core modules and subsequently purchasing additional applications over time. We also seek to increase adoption within existing customer organizations through product innovation, customer success programs, and industry-specific functionality.

Our industry is highly competitive and rapidly evolving. We compete with larger, more established software vendors, other cloud-native providers, and specialized point solution companies. We believe our focus on the mid-market, combined with our unified architecture and customer-centric deployment model, positions us well to continue to grow. At the same time, we operate in a dynamic environment that requires ongoing investment in research and development, security, infrastructure, and talent.

We were incorporated in the State of Delaware on June 12, 2014. Our corporate headquarters are located at 8200 Congress Avenue, Suite 400, Austin, Texas 78701, and our telephone number is (512) 555-0100. Our website address is www.pinnaclesoftware.com. Information contained on, or accessible through, our website is not incorporated by reference into this prospectus, and you should not consider it part of this prospectus.

An investment in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. **[Risks Related to Our Business and Industry]{.underline}**

**We have a limited operating history as a public company, which makes it difficult to predict our future results.**

Although we have operated our business since 2014, we have not operated as a public company. As a public company, we will incur significant legal, accounting, compliance, and other expenses that we did not incur as a private company. We will also be required to implement additional internal controls, procedures, and disclosure practices. These requirements may place significant demands on management and finance personnel and could divert attention from other business concerns. In addition, our limited experience operating as a public company may make it difficult for investors to evaluate our future prospects.

**We face intense competition from larger, more established software companies, including providers of legacy on-premise ERP and CRM solutions as well as other cloud-based competitors.**

The markets for ERP and CRM software are highly competitive and rapidly evolving. We compete against large enterprise software vendors with significantly greater financial, technical, marketing, and other resources, as well as newer cloud-based providers and specialized point-solution vendors. Some of our competitors may be able to devote greater resources to product development, sales and marketing, pricing, support, and strategic relationships than we can. Competitive pressures may result in price reductions, reduced margins, longer sales cycles, and loss of market share.

**Our growth depends on our ability to attract new customers and retain and expand revenue from existing customers.**

Our future growth depends on our ability to continue to add new customers and expand our relationships with existing customers. If we are unable to maintain or increase sales to new and existing customers, our revenue growth may slow. Customer retention and expansion depend on many factors, including our product functionality, customer support, pricing, security, reliability, and ability to deliver measurable value. If customers fail to renew subscriptions, reduce the scope of their subscriptions, or do not expand their usage over time, our business may be harmed.

**We may not be able to successfully develop and market new products and features.**

Our success depends in part on our ability to anticipate market needs and develop, enhance, and introduce new products, features, and functionality in a timely manner. The development process is complex and costly, and our efforts may not result in commercially successful products. We may make errors in product planning, fail to address customer needs, or misjudge competitive trends. If we are unable to successfully innovate, our competitive position may weaken.

**Failure to manage our growth effectively could harm our business.**

We have experienced rapid growth in our business, headcount, customer base, and operations. Continued growth could place significant strain on our management, administrative, operational, and financial infrastructure. To manage growth effectively, we must continue to improve our systems, controls, and processes, and we must attract, retain, and integrate qualified personnel. If we fail to manage our growth effectively, our business and results of operations could be adversely affected.

**Our business depends on the reliable performance of our cloud platform.**

Our customers depend on our platform to manage important business processes, and any disruption in the availability, performance, or functionality of our services could result in customer dissatisfaction, reputational damage, contractual claims, and lost revenue. Our platform may be subject to interruptions caused by software defects, capacity constraints, cyber incidents, natural disasters, power outages, telecommunications failures, or other events. We may not be able to detect or mitigate all such problems before they result in service degradation or outage.

**If we fail to maintain and enhance our brand, our ability to attract customers could be impaired.**

We believe that maintaining and enhancing the Pinnacle brand is important to attracting new customers, partners, and employees. Brand promotion activities may not be successful or may not generate a meaningful return on investment. Harm to our brand may arise from product issues, service disruptions, security concerns, negative publicity, or actions by our competitors. If we fail to maintain and enhance our brand, our business may be harmed.

**We rely on third-party data center providers and cloud computing platforms.**

We depend on third-party hosting infrastructure and cloud service providers to operate our business. If these providers experience outages, capacity limitations, security incidents, or other disruptions, our ability to provide services to customers may be impaired. We may also face increased costs, changes in service terms, or vendor concentration risks. Our customers may hold us responsible for service interruptions even when caused by third-party providers.

**Our sales cycles can be long and unpredictable.**

The sale of our solutions often involves significant time, effort, and expense and may require approvals from multiple stakeholders within a prospective customer organization. Sales cycles may be extended by budget constraints, customer evaluation processes, competing priorities, information security reviews, implementation concerns, and macroeconomic conditions. A delay or failure in closing expected transactions could adversely affect our quarterly and annual results.

**Seasonal fluctuations in our business could cause variability in our results.**

We have experienced and may continue to experience seasonal fluctuations in our sales and operating results. Our new customer bookings have historically been stronger in the fourth quarter due to customer budget cycles, while implementation activity may vary by industry and customer timing. Seasonal trends may be affected by changes in our business, market conditions, and the broader economy. As a result, comparisons of our results from period to period may not be meaningful.

**We may pursue acquisitions, investments, or strategic alliances, which could divert management\'s attention or prove difficult to integrate.**

We may in the future pursue acquisitions, investments, or strategic partnerships to expand our business, product offerings, or capabilities. Such transactions involve numerous risks, including difficulties integrating operations, technologies, personnel, and cultures; failure to achieve expected synergies; assumption of liabilities; and diversion of management attention. We may also issue equity or incur debt in connection with such transactions. If we fail to successfully identify, consummate, or integrate acquisitions or other strategic initiatives, our business could be adversely affected.

**Our professional services revenue has lower margins than our subscription revenue.**

We derive a portion of our revenue from professional services, including implementation, training, and customization. Professional services generally have lower gross margins than subscription revenue and may require significant personnel and partner resources. If professional services revenue represents a larger-than-expected portion of our overall revenue, or if we are unable to manage delivery costs effectively, our gross margins and operating results may be adversely affected.

**[Risks Related to Our Technology and Intellectual Property]{.underline}**

**We may be unable to protect our intellectual property rights.**

Our success depends in part on our ability to protect our proprietary technology and intellectual property. We rely on a combination of patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, confidentiality agreements, and other contractual restrictions. These measures may be inadequate. Unauthorized parties may attempt to copy, reverse engineer, misappropriate, or otherwise obtain and use our technology. Litigation to protect our intellectual property may be costly and time-consuming and may not be successful.

**We may be subject to claims of intellectual property infringement by third parties.**

The software industry is characterized by frequent claims and litigation relating to intellectual property rights. We may in the future be subject to claims that our products, services, or technologies infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate patents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, or other intellectual property rights of third parties. Even claims without merit can be costly to defend, require significant management attention, and result in reputational harm. If we are required to pay damages, obtain licenses, modify our products, or stop using certain technology, our business could be materially harmed.

**Our software may contain undetected errors or defects.**

Our software is complex and may contain undetected defects, errors, vulnerabilities, or performance problems. These issues may be discovered only after commercial release and could result in loss of or delay in market acceptance, harm to our reputation, loss of revenue, increased warranty or support costs, or liability claims. We may not have adequate insurance coverage for such claims.

**Security breaches, cyberattacks, or other incidents affecting our systems or data could harm our reputation and business.**

Our platform processes and stores sensitive business information and, in some cases, personal data on behalf of our customers. We also collect and store confidential information about our business and employees. Our systems and those of our service providers may be vulnerable to cyberattacks, unauthorized access, ransomware, phishing, denial-of-service attacks, malware, insider threats, software vulnerabilities, and other security incidents. Any actual or perceived compromise of security could result in litigation, regulatory investigations, indemnity obligations, contract claims, remediation costs, reputational harm, customer loss, and operational disruption.

**We use open-source software in our products, which could subject us to litigation or other actions.**

We use open-source software in connection with our products and internal systems. The terms of certain open-source licenses may require us to make source code available, grant broader rights to third parties, or otherwise impose obligations that we do not intend. If we fail to comply with applicable open-source licenses, we could be required to release proprietary source code, incur litigation costs, or cease distributing affected software.

**Interruptions or delays in our hosting and cloud services could adversely affect our business.**

Because our applications are hosted and delivered over the internet, customers depend on the continuous availability of our services. Interruptions or delays due to third-party service providers, software defects, infrastructure failures, or external events could impair our ability to serve customers. Such disruptions may result in refunds, service credits, customer dissatisfaction, and reputational harm.

**We have incurred net losses in prior periods and may not achieve or maintain profitability in the future.**

Although we generated operating income in fiscal 2020 and net income in the six months ended June 30, 2021, we have incurred net losses in prior periods and may not sustain profitability. We expect to continue to invest substantially in product development, infrastructure, sales, marketing, and compliance. These investments may adversely affect our operating results in the near term. If our revenue growth slows or if our expenses increase more than expected, we may not be able to maintain profitability.

**Our indebtedness under our bridge credit facility may limit our operational flexibility.**

Our indebtedness may reduce our ability to invest in our business, increase our vulnerability to economic downturns, and limit our flexibility in planning for or reacting to changes in our industry. **Fluctuations in our quarterly results of operations may cause our stock price to decline.**

Our quarterly operating results may fluctuate significantly as a result of many factors, including the timing of customer bookings and implementations, sales cycles, seasonality, customer renewals, mix of subscription and services revenue, pricing changes, operating expense levels, and general economic conditions. As a result, period-to-period comparisons may not be meaningful, and our results may fall below the expectations of investors or analysts.

**If we fail to maintain an effective system of internal controls, we may not be able to accurately report our financial results.**

As a public company, we will be required to maintain internal control over financial reporting and disclosure controls and procedures that satisfy the requirements of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. Effective internal controls are necessary for us to produce reliable financial statements and to prevent fraud. We may identify control deficiencies that must be remediated, and the process of designing and implementing effective controls is time-consuming and costly. If we fail to maintain effective internal controls, we may be unable to accurately report financial results or prevent fraud, and investor confidence may decline.

**We may require additional capital to fund our operations and growth.**

We may need to raise additional capital in the future to support growth initiatives, product development, working capital needs, or strategic transactions. Additional financing may not be available on favorable terms or at all. If we raise funds through equity issuances, existing stockholders may experience dilution. If we raise funds through debt financing, we may become subject to additional restrictions and repayment obligations.

**An active trading market for our common stock may not develop or be sustained.**

Prior to this offering, there has been no public market for our common stock. Although we have been approved to list our common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market, an active trading market may not develop or be sustained following this offering. If one or more of the analysts who cover us downgrade our stock or publish unfavorable research, our stock price could decline. If few analysts commence or continue coverage of us, demand for our common stock could decrease and our stock price and trading volume could decline.

**[Overview]{.underline}**

Pinnacle Software Holdings, Inc. provides cloud-based ERP and CRM software solutions purpose-built for mid-market businesses. Our software is delivered on a subscription basis through a cloud-native, multi-tenant architecture. Our customers use our applications to manage core operational, financial, sales, marketing, customer service, and workflow processes. We generate substantially all of our revenue from software subscriptions and related professional services.

We believe the market opportunity for our solutions is significant. Mid-market organizations often require robust functionality and industry-specific configurability but may lack the resources or tolerance for the complexity associated with legacy enterprise systems. Our unified platform is designed to address these needs by providing integrated applications, rapid implementation, and a lower total cost of ownership.

Our business model is characterized by a high proportion of recurring subscription revenue, long-term customer relationships, and a land-and-expand sales strategy. We typically enter into annual and multi-year contracts, and our sales efforts focus on both new customer acquisition and expansion within our installed base. As of June 30, 2021, we served over 2,400 customers and employed approximately 1,850 people. Our net revenue retention rate as of June 30, 2021 was 118%.

**[Key Business Metrics]{.underline}**

We monitor a number of financial and operational metrics to evaluate our performance, identify trends, and guide business decisions.

**Annual Recurring Revenue**

Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, represents the annualized value of our active subscription contracts as of a given date, assuming any contract that expires during the next 12 months is renewed on existing terms. We use ARR as a key measure of the scale, growth, and predictability of our subscription business. As of June 30, 2021, our ARR was approximately \$310 million.

**Net Revenue Retention Rate**

We calculate net revenue retention rate as of a period end by dividing the ARR from customers that were customers as of the prior year period end by the ARR from those same customers as of the current period end, including the impact of upsells, downsells, churn, and contractions. As of June 30, 2021, our net revenue retention rate was 118%.

**Customers with More Than \$100,000 of ARR**

We define customers with more than \$100,000 of ARR as those active customers whose annualized subscription revenue at a given date exceeds \$100,000. This metric helps us evaluate our penetration of larger mid-market accounts. As of June 30, 2021, we had 385 customers with more than \$100,000 of ARR.
